data: Do all 19th-century poems have an arousal score of over 3.5?

The scatter plot shows the distribution of arousal scores across different time periods. The x-axis represents the publication year, and the y-axis represents the arousal score. The data points are color-coded based on the time period: light blue for 19th-century poems, dark blue for contemporary poems, and black triangles for Imagist poems. The caption indicates that following the Imagist movement, poems scored increasingly lower on emotional arousal.

To determine if all 19th-century poems have an arousal score of over 3.5, we need to examine the data points for 19th-century poems. From the scatter plot, it is clear that some 19th-century poems have an arousal score below 3.5. Therefore, not all 19th-century poems have an arousal score of over 3.5.
